key_insight: A large language model, with Lean 4 verification, produced a machine-checked proof of the long-open FGG conjecture for depth-p QAOA on the ring of disagrees, yielding the exact ratio (2p+1)/(2p+2).
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a practical AI-plus-formal-methods workflow for solving and certifying difficult quantum-optimization proofs, strengthening trust in results used to guide quantum algorithm design.
method: Formalized the QAOA problem and the known results in Lean 4 using an existing quantum-information library.
Reduced the conjecture to a single open mathematical statement, then let the model construct the missing proof in Lean.
Closed the loop between natural-language reasoning and mechanical verification until the proof was certified end-to-end.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an end-to-end machine-verified proof in Lean 4 of an open conjecture, with the model uncovering a hidden dynamical symmetry to complete the argument.
watch_item: The result depends on the correctness of the formalization scaffolding and the underlying Lean library, so encoding errors or assumptions could still affect the interpretation.
paper_title: A Machine-Verified Proof of a Quantum-Optimization Conjecture
